Definition 3.3 (First-Order Zero-Chain) . A differentiable function $H:\mathbb{R}^{T}\to\mathbb{R}$ is a first-order zero-chain if $\operatorname{prog}_{0}(\nabla H(u))\leq\operatorname{prog}_{0}(u)+1\qquad\text{for every }u\in\mathbb{R}^{T}.$

Definition 3.4 (Probability- $p$ Zero-Chain) . Let $p\in(0,1]$ , and let $g_{H}(u;\xi)$ be an unbiased gradient estimator of $H$ . We call $g_{H}$ a probability- $p$ zero-chain (PZC) if $\displaystyle\mathbb{P}_{\xi}\!\left(\exists u\in\mathbb{R}^{T}:\operatorname{prog}_{0}(g_{H}(u;\xi))=\operatorname{prog}_{1/4}(u)+1\right)$ $\displaystyle\leq p,$ (20) $\displaystyle\mathbb{P}_{\xi}\!\left(\exists u\in\mathbb{R}^{T}:\operatorname{prog}_{0}(g_{H}(u;\xi))>\operatorname{prog}_{1/4}(u)+1\right)$ $\displaystyle=0.$

Theorem 4.1 (Bounded Variance) . There are universal constants $c,c_{0}>0$ such that, for $L,\mu,\Delta>0$ , $\sigma\geq 0$ , $\kappa=L/\mu\geq 8$ , and $0<{\epsilon}^{2}\leq c_{0}L\Delta$ , $\mathcal{C}_{{\epsilon},{\rm zr}}^{(1)}\bigl(\mathcal{I}_{\rm BV}(L,\mu,\Delta,\sigma)\bigr)\geq c\frac{L\Delta}{{\epsilon}^{2}}\max\left\{1,\frac{\kappa\sigma^{2}}{{\epsilon}^{2}}\right\}.$ (21) The same order holds for the expected-norm target. The hard instances have actual smoothness-to-strong-concavity ratio within universal constant factors of $\kappa$ .

Theorem 5.1 (Averaged Smoothness) . There are universal constants $c,c_{0},c_{1}>0$ such that the following holds for every fixed finite $K\geq 1$ . Let $\overline{L},\mu,\Delta>0$ , $\sigma\geq 0$ , $\kappa=\overline{L}/\mu\geq 8$ , and suppose $0<{\epsilon}^{2}\leq c_{0}\overline{L}\Delta,\qquad{\epsilon}\sigma\leq c_{1}\overline{L}\Delta\sqrt{\kappa}.$ (23) Then $\mathcal{C}_{{\epsilon},{\rm zr}}^{(K)}\bigl(\mathcal{I}_{\rm AS}(\overline{L},\mu,\Delta,\sigma)\bigr)\geq c\frac{\overline{L}\Delta}{{\epsilon}^{2}}\max\left\{1,\min\left\{\frac{\kappa\sigma^{2}}{{\epsilon}^{2}},\frac{\kappa^{3/2}\sigma}{{\epsilon}}\right\}\right\}.$ (24) The same order holds for the expected-norm target.

Corollary 5.2 (Moreau Envelope Lower Bounds) . The lower bounds in Theorems 4.1 and 5.1 also hold, up to universal constant factors, when the required output satisfies either $\mathbb{E}\left\lVert\nabla P_{f}(\hat{x})\right\rVert^{2}\leq{\epsilon}^{2}\qquad\text{or}\qquad\mathbb{E}\left\lVert\nabla P_{f}(\hat{x})\right\rVert\leq{\epsilon}.$ Here the parameters, oracle protocols, and algorithm class are unchanged.
